They are a best guess from the vendor name (a MAC prefix identifies the manufacturer, not the product line): check the flagged ones. The rules are created below your own rules (negative priority); types set by hand are never changed.

macVendors.pageDesc: Browse the IEEE OUI database and set custom vendor name overrides.
macVendors.infoDesc: Setting a custom name replaces the IEEE vendor name in device views. Clearing the override restores the original IEEE name. Overrides survive future OUI database reseeds.
macVendors.infoBody: When a probe discovers a device, the first 3 octets of the MAC address are looked up here. If you set a custom override, that name is shown in the site device list and used in vendor-based type classification rules. Refresh from IEEE downloads the latest OUI CSV (~30 000 entries) and upserts everything — your custom overrides are always preserved.
macVendors.pageIntro: Browse the IEEE OUI database and override vendor names for specific MAC prefixes. Custom names are used when identifying devices on sites.
macVendors.refreshHint: Download the latest IEEE OUI CSV and upsert all entries. Custom overrides are preserved.
macVendors.overrideHint: Leave empty to use the IEEE name again.
macVendors.infoBodyRegistry: When a probe discovers a device, its MAC address is looked up here by the longest registered prefix (MA-S 36 bits, then MA-M 28 bits, then MA-L 24 bits). If you set a custom override, that name is shown in the site device list and used in vendor-based type classification rules. The server downloads the IEEE registries by itself on a fresh install and every 30 days; Refresh registry does it now. Your custom overrides are always preserved.
macVendors.refreshRegistryHint: Download the latest IEEE registries (MA-L, MA-M, MA-S) and upsert all entries. Custom overrides are preserved. The server also refreshes them by itself every 30 days.

download.pageDesc: Download the Oblimap desktop app or network probe binary.
download.title: Obli.tools
download.description:
A lightweight native interface that groups all your Obli apps into one window.
Get sound notifications and a distraction-free monitoring experience.
download.buildFromSourceDesc: The desktop app lives in the desktop-app/ directory of the Oblimap repository.
download.step1: On first launch, enter your Obliview server URL. Linked apps (Obliguard, Oblimap, Obliance) are discovered automatically.
download.step2: Each app opens in its own native tab — no browser overhead, no address bar, sessions are preserved when switching tabs.
download.step3: Sound notifications play when a probe goes down/up or an agent threshold is breached/cleared.
download.step4: Click the ⚙ gear icon (bottom-right corner) to change the server URL at any time.
download.step5: No rebuild is needed after Oblimap updates — the app always loads the latest web UI.

features.soundAlerts: Sound alerts for probe down / recovery
features.agentAlerts: Push notifications for new device discoveries

probe.title: Oblimap Network Probe
probe.description: A lightweight scanner that discovers and monitors devices on a local network segment. Deploy one probe per subnet.
probe.buildFromSourceDesc: The probe source lives in the probe/ directory of the Oblimap repository. Build with go build -o oblimap-probe .
probe.step1: Run the probe binary on any machine inside the target network segment.
probe.step2: The probe registers itself with your Oblimap server using an API key from the admin panel.
probe.step3: An admin approves the probe and assigns it to a site.
probe.step4: The probe scans the network on a configurable interval and reports discovered devices.
probe.step5: Devices appear automatically in the site, tracked by MAC address across IP changes.

download.buildFromSourceDetail: It is a Go application using the native OS webview (WebView2 on Windows, WKWebView on macOS). On Windows run .\build-windows.ps1 (requires WiX v4: dotnet tool install --global wix). On macOS run ./build-mac.sh.

addProbe.mikrotikStep2: 2. Paste in the router terminal. The password of the read-only "oblimap" user was generated for this router; adapt the 172.17.0.0/24 subnet and the oblimap/ disk paths when needed (e.g. usb1/oblimap on small flash).
